**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4,
the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, the identical-particle
and spin postulate P6, and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Fix a mass parameter
$m>0$ and a spin label $s=0$, so that the framework's one-particle model
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] reads its state space as
$H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with the pairing linear in the first
argument, its componentwise position family $Q_{1},Q_{2},Q_{3}$, its
componentwise momentum family $P_{1},P_{2},P_{3}$ and the action constant
$\hbar>0$; the spin-zero internal factor carries the trivial representation of
P6. Units are those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]: position is
read in metres, momentum in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, energy and potential
energy in joules, and $\hbar$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) The declared central-potential model.** As an additional model
assumption of the pair, adopt the **central-potential model**. Its declared
state space is $H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ of clause (a), with the
position and momentum families $Q_{j}$, $P_{k}$ of that clause
([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]). A **declared central
potential** of the model is a function $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ of the
form $V(x):=v(|x|)$ for $x\ne0$, where $v:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is real,
bounded and measurable and $\|V\|_{\infty}:=\|v\|_{\infty}=\sup_{r>0}|v(r)|$ is
finite; the assignment $V(0):=0$ is a declared convention that does not affect
the $L^{2}$ theory. The potential energy is read in joules. The model declares
the **Born position law** of the framework for a unit class $\psi$,
$$\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B):=\int_{B}|\psi(x)|^{2}\,dx\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}\ \text{Borel}),$$
the spin-zero reading of clause (b) of
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]]. The pair asserts no derivation
of a central force law from $H_{0}$ or from P5: the restriction to a declared
central potential is an assumption of the model, and an assignment of a
concrete material system to the model is an identification in the sense of
clause (iii) of P7 and carries the corresponding uncertainty.

**(c) The assigned energy operator.** Let $\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary
Plancherel transform of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b), $c:=2\pi^{2}\hbar^{2}/m$, and let
$$H_{0}^{\mathrm{free}}:=\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{c|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2},\qquad D(H_{0}^{\mathrm{free}}):=\bigl\{f\in H_{0}:|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in H_{0}\bigr\}$$
be the free operator of that clause with $d=3$ and $b=0$. With $M_{V}$ the
bounded multiplication operator of clause (a) of the same theorem, the
**assigned energy operator** of the model with central potential $V$ is
$$H_{V}:=H_{0}^{\mathrm{free}}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V}):=D(H_{0}^{\mathrm{free}}).$$
The declared energy unit is the joule. By clause (c) of the cited theorem
$H_{V}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{V})$, bounded below by $-\|V\|_{\infty}$; by
[[lem-nrqm-central-free-operator-differential-identification]] the domain is
the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and
$$H_{V}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f+Vf\qquad(f\in D(H_{V})),$$
$\Delta_{w}=D_{1}^{2}+D_{2}^{2}+D_{3}^{2}$ the weak Laplacian of that lemma, so
that on any open set on which $V$ is of class $C^{2}$ the model's
time-independent equation is the ordinary differential equation
$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta\psi+V\psi=E\psi$ for a $C^{2}$ representative. The
model adopts $(H_{V},\mathrm J)$ as its declared energy observable; its
self-adjointness is the cited theorem's, and no further spectral property is
presupposed here.

**(d) The declared spherical reading.** Let $U$ be the unitary of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-angular-radial-unitary-reduction]] from
$H_{0}$ onto $K=\bigoplus_{(l,m)}L^{2}((0,\infty),dr;\mathbb C)$, written
$U\psi=(u_{lm})_{l\ge0,-l\le m\le l}$, and let $(Y_{lm})$ be the complete
orthonormal family of that theorem. As an additional reading of the model, the
pair declares the **spherical sector** $(l,m)$ and the **effective potential**
$$v^{\mathrm{eff}}_{l}(r):=v(r)+\frac{\hbar^{2}l(l+1)}{2mr^{2}}\qquad(r>0),$$
whose second summand is called the **angular-momentum barrier**; both
summands, and $v^{\mathrm{eff}}_{l}$, are read in joules. The model's
**declared radial equation** in the sector $(l,m)$ is the eigenvalue equation
for the one-dimensional expression
$$u\longmapsto-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}u''+\Bigl(v(r)+\frac{\hbar^{2}l(l+1)}{2mr^{2}}\Bigr)u,\qquad u:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb C,$$
restricted to declared admissible classes (for instance $u\in
C_{c}^{\infty}((0,\infty))$). The pair does not presuppose that the assigned
energy operator of clause (c) literally reduces to this expression; the
consistency of the two readings on smooth states is the content of the
spherical-reduction theorem of this page, which is proved from the cited
mathematics. The angular-momentum quantum numbers $l$ and $m$
appearing in the reading are labels of the orthonormal family $(Y_{lm})$; the
identification of $l$ with a total angular momentum of a material system is a
separate assignment of the framework's angular-momentum items and is not made
here.

**(e) Stationary and bound-state vocabulary.** A **stationary vector** of the
model with potential $V$ and **energy** $E\in\mathbb R$ is a nonzero class
$\psi\in D(H_{V})$ with $H_{V}\psi=E\psi$; the pair $(\psi,E)$ is an
**eigenpair** of the model. A **bound state** of the model is a stationary
vector with energy $E<0$ whose representative is normalised, $\|\psi\|=1$; its
eigenvalue is its **binding energy**, read in joules, and the value $0$ is
called the **continuum threshold** of the model. The model reads the energy
outcome law of the pure preparation of a unit eigenvector with eigenvalue $E$
as the point mass $\delta_{E}$, the reading of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the
position density of that preparation as $|\psi|^{2}$ by clause (b). These are
declarations of the model under P2; they construct no sample, detector or
measured value, and they assert no stability, decay or formation claim.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the data of the pair: a declared
state space, position and momentum assignments, an assigned energy operator
for a real bounded measurable central potential, a declared spherical reading
with its effective potential and radial equation, and a stationary-state and
bound-state vocabulary. They introduce no assumption beyond P1, P2, P4, P5,
P6, P7 and the cited mathematics; in particular the central form of the
potential, the model's use of the full three-dimensional space as its state
space and the identification of the spherical sectors with angular-momentum
labels are declarations of the pair. The model excludes from its scope, until
their own items introduce them: the Coulomb potential $\propto-1/r$ and other
unbounded or singular potentials; spin and magnetic couplings; relativistic
corrections; finite nuclear size; the radiation extension, spontaneous
emission and radiation reaction; external electromagnetic fields; and any
many-body or shielding modification of a central potential. No numerical value
of $m$, $\hbar$ or of any potential is fixed here, and no empirical result is
asserted.

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the framework data of clause (a) of the declared
central-potential model [[def-nrqm-central-framework-central-potential-model]]
with a declared mass parameter $m>0$, spin label $s=0$, the state space
$H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the componentwise position and momentum
families and the action constant $\hbar>0$ of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]; units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) The declared one-centre Coulomb model.** As an additional model
assumption of the pair, fix a real **coupling** $\kappa>0$ with the declared
unit $\mathrm{J\,m}$ and put
$$\gamma:=\frac{2m\kappa}{\hbar^{2}}\qquad(\text{unit }\mathrm{m^{-1}}),\qquad C_{\gamma}:=-\Delta-\frac{\gamma}{|\cdot|}\ \text{ on }\ D(C_{\gamma})=H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C),$$
the self-adjoint operator of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]] clause (c). The **assigned
energy operator** of the one-centre Coulomb model is
$$H_{\kappa}:=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\,C_{\gamma},$$
with domain $D(H_{\kappa}):=D(C_{\gamma})$; by
[[lem-nrqm-potentials-positive-scaling-of-self-adjoint-operators]] clauses (a)
and (b) it is self-adjoint with the same domain, and by
[[lem-nrqm-central-free-operator-differential-identification]] together with
the action formula of the cited theorem it acts by
$$H_{\kappa}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f-\kappa\frac{f}{|\cdot|}\qquad(f\in D(H_{\kappa})),$$
where $\Delta_{w}$ is the weak Laplacian. The model declares the **length
scale** $a_{\kappa}:=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)$, read in metres, and the **energy
scale** $\mathcal E_{\kappa}:=m\kappa^{2}/(2\hbar^{2})=\hbar^{2}/(2ma_{\kappa}^{2})$,
read in joules. The model adopts $(H_{\kappa},\mathrm J)$ as its declared
energy observable for the one-centre problem; the self-adjointness is the
cited theorem's and no spectral property is presupposed here.

**(c) The declared radial reading of the one-centre model.** Let $U$ and
$(A_{l})_{l\ge0}$ be the unitary and the radial operators of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]] clauses (a)-(d):
$U$ maps $H_{0}$ onto $K=\bigoplus_{(l,m)}L^{2}((0,\infty),dr;\mathbb C)$ with
$UH_{\kappa}U^{*}=\bigoplus_{(l,m)}(\hbar^{2}/2m)A_{l}$, and each $A_{l}$ is self-adjoint
with form domain $V_{l}$ and domain $D(A_{l})$. The model declares the
**sector $(l,m)$ radial energy operator** $A_{l}^{(\kappa)}:=(\hbar^{2}/2m)A_{l}$,
read in joules, and, for a class $u\in D(A_{l})$, the **declared radial
equation** is the distributional identity
$$-u''(r)+\Bigl(\frac{l(l+1)}{r^{2}}-\frac{\gamma}{r}\Bigr)u(r)=A_{l}u(r)\qquad\text{on }(0,\infty),$$
which by clause (c) of the cited theorem is an ordinary differential equation
with $C^{2}$ representative whenever $A_{l}u=Eu$ for a constant $E$. The
**regular reduced solution** at energy attribute $k>0$ is the function
$u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)=r^{l+1}e^{-kr}v(2kr)$ of clause (c) of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-kummer-recurrence-and-termination]], with $v$ the regular
power series of that clause; the pair uses it as the declared radial template
of the model, not as a physical state, until the normalisation and spectral
theorems of the page identify it.

**(d) The declared two-body Coulomb model.** As a further model assumption,
take two **distinguishable** spinless massive particles with declared mass
parameters $m_{1},m_{2}>0$ (unit kg) and opposite declared charges: particle 1
carries $-q$ and particle 2 carries $+q$, with a real **charge parameter**
$q>0$ (unit C). Declare the **pair coupling**
$$\kappa:=\frac{q^{2}}{4\pi\varepsilon_{0}},\qquad \varepsilon_{0}:=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1},$$
where $\mu_{0}$ is the declared magnetic constant of the SI conventions and
$c$ the speed of light, both as in clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the identification $\kappa=q^{2}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$
is a constitutive assumption of the model, and $\kappa$ is read in
$\mathrm{J\,m}$. The two-particle state space is the Hilbert tensor product of
two copies of the one-particle space of clause (a) as in
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], identified with
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{6};\mathbb C)$ through
[[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]; the spin-zero internal
factor is trivial, and because the two particles are of different species no
symmetrisation is imposed (the case of identical species belongs to the
identical-particle sector of P6 and is not used here). The **assigned energy
operator** is
$$H_{2}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m_{1}}\Delta_{x_{1}}-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m_{2}}\Delta_{x_{2}}-\frac{\kappa}{|x_{1}-x_{2}|},\qquad D(H_{2}):=H^{2}(\mathbb R^{6};\mathbb C),$$
which is self-adjoint by clause (c) of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-two-body-reduced-mass]]. Let
$$\Phi(x_{1},x_{2}):=(R,r),\qquad R:=\frac{m_{1}x_{1}+m_{2}x_{2}}{M},\quad r:=x_{1}-x_{2},\quad M:=m_{1}+m_{2},$$
be the centre-of-mass/relative coordinate map of that theorem, with its
unitary $U_{\Phi}$. The model declares the **centre-of-mass/relative reading**
$U_{\Phi}H_{2}U_{\Phi}^{-1}=T_{R}\otimes I+I\otimes C_{\mu}$ of clause (c) of
that theorem, with the **reduced mass**
$$\mu:=\frac{m_{1}m_{2}}{m_{1}+m_{2}}\qquad(\text{unit }\mathrm{kg}),$$
the centre-of-mass kinetic operator $T_{R}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2M}\Delta_{R}$
and the **relative operator** $C_{\mu}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2\mu}\Delta_{r}-\frac{\kappa}{|r|}$;
the relative operator is exactly the one-centre Coulomb operator of clause
(b) with mass parameter $\mu$. The model further declares the **fixed-nucleus
reading**: the one-centre model of clauses (b), (c) with mass parameter $m_{1}$
is read as the limiting description in which the second particle is
infinitely heavy, $\mu\to m_{1}$ as $m_{2}\to\infty$ at fixed $m_{1},\kappa$;
this is a declared limiting reading, and no convergence theorem for operators
or states is asserted by it.

**(e) The hydrogen-like identification.** A **hydrogen-like ion** assignment of
the two-body model is the choice $m_{1}=m_{\mathrm e}$ (electron mass
parameter), $m_{2}=m_{\mathrm n}$ (nuclear mass parameter) and $q=e$ (the
elementary charge of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]) with nuclear charge $+Ze$, so that
$\kappa=Ze^{2}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$ for a declared positive integer $Z$;
$Z=1$ with a proton mass parameter $m_{\mathrm p}$ is the **hydrogen
assignment**. These assignments use empirical mass and charge parameters; any
comparison of the model's consequences with a laboratory hydrogen atom is a
tested identification in the sense of clause (iii) of P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]) and carries the
uncertainty of that identification. The model declares no numerical value of
$m_{\mathrm e},m_{\mathrm n},e,\mu_{0}$ or $\hbar$; numerical evaluations, when
made, use their declared or measured values as explicitly qualified empirical
inputs.

**(f) Scope exclusions.** Until their own items introduce them, the Coulomb
and hydrogen models exclude: spin, magnetic moment couplings and
spin–statistics assignments beyond the trivial spin-zero factor; relativistic
corrections, in particular any fine-structure splitting of the degeneracy of
the gross-structure levels; finite nuclear size, nuclear recoil beyond the
two-body reduction of clause (d), and nuclear structure; QED corrections such
as vacuum polarisation and the Lamb shift, and hyperfine structure; shielding
and many-body modification of the $1/r$ potential; the radiation extension,
spontaneous emission, radiation reaction and any photon, transition-frequency
or line-intensity statement; external electromagnetic fields; and any
scattering, ionisation or continuum process, which belongs to the scattering
items of the quantum-mechanics track. The model asserts no empirical result
and fixes no measured quantity.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$(V,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_V)$ and $(H,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_H)$ be
complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-inner-product-space]]) and let $i:V\to H$ be a linear map with dense
image.

**Symmetric forms.** A *sesquilinear form on $V$* is a map
$a:V\times V\to\mathbb C$ that is linear in its first argument and
conjugate-linear in its second; it is *symmetric* if
$a(u,v)=\overline{a(v,u)}$ for all $u,v\in V$, in which case $a(u,u)\in\mathbb R$
and $\operatorname{Re}a(u,v)=\operatorname{Re}\overline{a(v,u)}$.

**Bounded and semibounded.** Such a form is *bounded* if there is $C>0$ with
$|a(u,v)|\le C\|u\|_V\|v\|_V$ for all $u,v\in V$, and *semibounded below with
bound $M\ge0$* if $a(u,u)\ge-M\|i(u)\|_H^2$ for every $u\in V$.

**Form seminorm and closedness.** Let $M\ge0$ be a bound as above and define the
*form seminorm*
$$\|u\|_{a,M}:=\Bigl(\operatorname{Re}a(u,u)+(M+1)\|i(u)\|_H^2\Bigr)^{1/2}\qquad(u\in V).$$
It is a seminorm because $a(u,v)+(M+1)\langle i(u),i(v)\rangle_H$ is a positive semidefinite Hermitian form; its Cauchy–Schwarz inequality follows by expanding its value on $u+tv$ and minimizing over the scalar $t$, and gives the triangle inequality. It need not separate points for a general dense-image map $i$. The form $a$ is *closed* if there are such an $M$ and constants $c,C>0$ with
$c\|u\|_V\le\|u\|_{a,M}\le C\|u\|_V$ for every $u\in V$; then
the form seminorm is a norm, and $(V,\|\cdot\|_{a,M})$ is complete because $V$ is. If $i$ is injective, it is already a norm before closedness, since its square is at least $\|i(u)\|_H^2$.

**Associated operator.** With $a$ and $i$ as above, define
$$D(A):=\Bigl\{u\in V:\ \text{there is }f\in H\text{ with }a(u,v)=\langle f,i(v)\rangle_H\text{ for every }v\in V\Bigr\},\qquad Au:=f .$$
The element $f$ is unique when it exists, because two candidates differ by an
element of $H$ orthogonal to the dense subspace $i(V)$, hence coincide;
$A$ is called the *operator associated with $a$*. This definition asserts
neither that $A$ is densely defined, nor that $A$ is symmetric, nor that $A$ is
self-adjoint or bounded below; the specific closed semibounded form of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]] establishes those
properties for its own associated operator by a direct computation. When $V$
is a subspace of $H$ and $i$ is the inclusion, $\|i(u)\|_H$ is written
$\|u\|_H$ and the pairing $\langle f,i(v)\rangle_H$ is written
$\langle f,v\rangle$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Write
$L^2=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ for the complex Hilbert space of Lebesgue
(equivalence classes of) square-integrable functions with inner product
$\langle f,g\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R^3}f\overline g$ linear in the first
argument ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-hilbert-space]]), and write $L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$
for the same construction over the product with Lebesgue measure.

**Kernel data.** Let $k\in L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$.

**Domain and action.** For $f\in L^2$ say that the integral defining $T_kf$
*exists at* $x\in\mathbb R^3$ if the function
$y\mapsto k(x,y)f(y)$ lies in $L^1(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, and at such points
put
$$(T_kf)(x):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}k(x,y)f(y)\,dy .$$
Define
$$D(T_k):=\Bigl\{f\in L^2:\ x\mapsto(T_kf)(x)\ \text{exists for almost every }x\text{ and agrees a.e. with a class in }L^2\Bigr\},$$
and for $f\in D(T_k)$ let $T_kf$ denote that class. The assignment
$f\mapsto T_kf$ is called the *$L^2$-kernel operator with kernel $k$*.

**Hilbert-Schmidt operators.** A linear operator $T$ on $L^2$ is called a
*Hilbert-Schmidt operator* if there is
$k\in L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ with $D(T)=D(T_k)$ and
$T=T_k$; such a $k$ is called an *$L^2$ kernel* of $T$.

This definition asserts nothing about whether $D(T_k)$ is all of $L^2$,
whether $T_k$ is bounded, or whether $T_k$ is compact; those properties are
proved in [[lem-nrqm-coulomb-ltwo-kernel-operators-bounded-and-compact]]. A
finite product kernel $\sum_{i=1}^nf_i(x)\overline{g_i(y)}$ with
$f_i,g_i\in L^2$ is also a class in $L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$,
as the same lemma records, so $T_k$ is defined for it whenever that membership
is used.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $m,\hbar>0$, put
$c:=2\pi^{2}\hbar^{2}/m$, and let $H_{0}$ be the free operator of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b) with $d=3$, this $c$ and $b=0$:
$$H_{0}:=\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{c|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2},\qquad D(H_{0}):=\bigl\{f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C):|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\bigr\},$$
where $\mathcal F_{2}$ is the unitary Plancherel transform of that theorem.
Let $D^{2}_{j}$ denote the second weak partial derivative in the $j$-th
coordinate, defined componentwise on the locally integrable classes of
$\mathbb R^{3}$ ([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]),
write $\Delta_{w}:=D^{2}_{1}+D^{2}_{2}+D^{2}_{3}$ for the weak Laplacian
(defined on the classes whose three second weak partial derivatives lie in
$L^{2}$), and let $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ be the Sobolev space
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). Then:

(a) $D(H_{0})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ as sets and
$$H_{0}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\,\Delta_{w}f\qquad\text{for every }f\in D(H_{0});$$
equivalently, $\mathcal F_{2}(H_{0}f)(\xi)=c|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f(\xi)$ and
$\mathcal F_{2}\bigl(-\tfrac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f\bigr)(\xi)=c|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f(\xi)$
for almost every $\xi$, and the two $L^{2}$ classes agree.

(b) For every real bounded measurable $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$, the
operator $H_{0}+M_{V}$ of clause (c) of the cited theorem, with domain
$D(H_{0})$, coincides with the operator $f\mapsto-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f+Vf$
on the same domain; in particular, for $E\in\mathbb R$ and
$\psi\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ the eigenvalue equation
$(H_{0}+M_{V})\psi=E\psi$ is equivalent to the weak equation
$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}\psi+V\psi=E\psi$ elementwise in
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$.

The statement identifies operators on the same domain; it asserts neither
smoothness of the classes in $W^{2,2}$ nor any physical interpretation.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,H',K,K'$ be complex Hilbert spaces and let $S\in\mathcal B(H,H')$, $T\in\mathcal B(K,K')$ be bounded linear operators ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Write $H\widehat\otimes K$ for the completion of the algebraic tensor product constructed in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], with inclusion $\kappa$.

(a) There is a unique bounded linear operator $S\otimes T: H\widehat\otimes K\to H'\widehat\otimes K'$ with $(S\otimes T)\kappa(u\otimes v)=\kappa'(Su\otimes Tv)$ for all $u\in H$, $v\in K$, and it satisfies $\|S\otimes T\|\le\|S\|\,\|T\|$ ([[def-operator-norm]]).

(b) For Hilbert spaces $H'',K''$ and bounded $S':H''\to H$, $T':K''\to K$, one has $(S\otimes T)(S'\otimes T')=(SS')\otimes(TT')$. In particular, for endomorphisms $S:H\to H$, $T:K\to K$, the endomorphisms $S\otimes I_K$ and $I_H\otimes T$ commute and their composite is $S\otimes T$.

(c) The Hilbert adjoint ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]) is $(S\otimes T)^*=S^*\otimes T^*$.

(d) If $S,T$ are unitary, then so is $S\otimes T$. No extension of unbounded maps, and no algebraic manipulation of domains of unbounded operators, is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). For $z\in\mathbb C$ with $\operatorname{Re}z>0$ and $n\ge1$ let

$V:=\mathbb C^2$ carry the standard inner product linear in the first argument, with orthonormal basis
$(e_+,e_-)$ where $e_+:=(1,0)$ and $e_-:=(0,1)$ ([[def-inner-product-space]]), and let $V^{\otimes n}$ be the
$n$-fold tensor power with the inner product of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] and place permutations $U_\pi$ ($\pi$ in the symmetric group
$S_n$, [[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]) of
[[def-commuting-symmetric-and-linear-actions-on-tensor-power]], with the diagonal action $W^{\otimes n}$ of
$W\in M_2(\mathbb C)$ and the operators
$\Delta(T):=\sum_{j=1}^{n}\mathbf 1^{\otimes(j-1)}\otimes T\otimes\mathbf 1^{\otimes(n-j)}$. Put

$$P_+:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}U_\pi,\qquad \mathcal S_n:=\operatorname{ran}P_+\subseteq V^{\otimes n},\qquad SU(2):=\{W\in M_2(\mathbb C): W^*W=I_2,\ \det W=1\},$$

where $W^*:=\overline W^{\mathsf T}$ is the conjugate transpose of $W$ and $I_2$ the identity matrix
([[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]], [[def-determinant-of-a-square-matrix]]). For $W\in SU(2)$ define
$U_n(W):=W^{\otimes n}|_{\mathcal S_n}$. For $k\in\{0,\dots,n\}$ let $s_k$ be the sum of the elementary tensors
$e_{\varepsilon_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{\varepsilon_n}$ over all $2^n$ strings
$(\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_n)\in\{+,-\}^n$ containing exactly $k$ entries $-$, and put
$v_k:=\binom nk^{-1/2}s_k$.

Then:

(a) $P_+$ is the orthogonal projection onto the closed subspace $\mathcal S_n$, $U_\pi$ and $W^{\otimes n}$ commute for
every $\pi\in S_n$ and every $W$, and $W^{\otimes n}(\mathcal S_n)\subseteq \mathcal S_n$; the assignment $W\mapsto U_n(W)$ is
well defined on all of $M_2(\mathbb C)$, and $U_n(W')U_n(W)=U_n(W'W)$ holds for all $W,W'$;

(b) $SU(2)$ is a subgroup of the multiplicative monoid of $M_2(\mathbb C)$ with identity $I_2$; for $W\in SU(2)$
the operator $U_n(W)$ is unitary with inverse $U_n(W^{-1})=U_n(W)^*$, so $U_n:SU(2)\to U(\mathcal S_n)$ is a group
homomorphism ([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]],
[[def-linear-isometry-and-orthogonal-or-unitary-operator]]);

(c) the vectors $v_0,\dots,v_n$ form an orthonormal basis of $\mathcal S_n$; in particular $\mathcal S_n$ is $(n+1)$-dimensional;

(d) the operators $J_i:=\tfrac12\Delta(\sigma_i)|_{\mathcal S_n}$, $i=x,y,z$, where $\sigma_x,\sigma_y,\sigma_z$ are the
Pauli matrices of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]], are self-adjoint and satisfy, with

$$J_zv_k=\bigl(\tfrac n2-k\bigr)v_k,\qquad J_+v_k=\sqrt{k(n-k+1)}\,v_{k-1},\qquad J_-v_k=\sqrt{(k+1)(n-k)}\,v_{k+1},$$

$v_k\mapsto e_{n/2-k}$ is a unitary equivalence of $(J_x,J_y,J_z)$ with the spin-$\tfrac n2$ matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]];

$A_i(s)A_i(t)=A_i(s+t)$ and $A_i'(0)=-\tfrac i2\sigma_i$, and $t\mapsto V_i(t):=U_n(A_i(t))$ is a strongly
continuous one-parameter unitary group on $\mathcal S_n$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]])
whose infinitesimal generator $G_i$ ([[def-infinitesimal-generator-of-a-unitary-group]]) is $G_i=-iJ_i$ on all
of $\mathcal S_n$; equivalently $\frac1t\bigl(V_i(t)v-v\bigr)\to-iJ_iv$ for every $v\in \mathcal S_n$;

$W_0\in SU(2)$, then $\|U_n(W_m)-U_n(W_0)\|\to0$ in the operator norm on $\mathcal S_n$.

generators. It does not assert that $SU(2)$ or any spin observable describes a physical particle, and it makes
no measurement or statistics claim.
